content.text:
The working tree is clean and all four commits are in. Here is the report.

## Commits (oldest → newest, all `Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`)

| Hash | Subject |
| --- | --- |
| `dc2c916ba` | `deck(process): one table for how each event kind travels` |
| `faca7b560` | `deck(process): luminous gates and comet trails, not slabs` |
| `8ecdedc36` | `deck(process): a camera that reads the run it is watching` |
| `3885e8743` | `deck(process): name the lanes in the panel as well as the scene` |

Each commit passed, before it was made: `pnpm --dir apps/command-deck build`, `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`, and `pnpm exec oxlint` on its changed files. No file outside my surface was touched (verified with `git diff --name-only e793c2842 HEAD`).

## What changed, per file

**`deck/pipeline.ts`** — the pipeline now runs along **+x with lanes spread across z** (`laneZ` replaces `laneY`), and carries the scene metrics every part measures against (`PIPELINE`: rail span, rail/floor y, gate top, gate margin). `STAGES` gained a `color` taken from the roster edge kind each gate performs (`verifies`/`judges`/`merges`), so a gate and the relationship it stands for are the same colour across the deck. `discoverLanes` now returns a `Lane[]` carrying the **roster name of the agent that emitted most of the lane's work**, every agent seen on the lane (for the activity clock), and a colour: the division colour, **spread across an 84° hue band when one division owns several lanes**, so six code-safety departments in one pink division stay apart. New: `flightOf` (an event at Integration is drawn arriving from Judging — a merge is only seen landing), `laneTotals`, `pipelineHalfWidth`.

**`components/process/kinds.ts`** (new) — one entry per `EventKind`: colour, head size, flight time, trail width and length, arc height. The scene and the panel legend read the same table; a finding takes its severity colour.

**`components/process/materials.ts`** (new) — the five additive shader materials: the view-space-widened **ribbon trail**, the one-mesh **lane rails** (per-vertex colour/gain, end fades), the gate **glass pane**, the gate **floor pool**, and the **time plane**. Each brightness uniform is handed back as a typed `IUniform<number>` so the frame loop never looks it up.

**`components/process/heat.ts`** (new) — the mutable frame state the layers share (gate arrival clocks, a ring queue, `merged`, `completed`). Held in a memo, read from `useFrame`, never React state.

**`components/process/Gates.tsx`** (new) — each stage is a **tall glass gate**: four additive edge bars, a pane, a floor pool on the grid, and a crisp `Html` label above the top beam. Rest dim → flare on arrival → Integration holds a steady glow once a merge lands or the run ends. Plus the shared **ring pool** (7 meshes) that drains the queue: a certificate rings at Verification, a merge at Integration, and a finished run rings once.

**`components/process/Ground.tsx`** (new) — the floor grid receding into fog; the **rails** (one mesh, one strip + one halo per lane, gain rewritten per frame from `store.activity`); the **lane labels** (agent name + event count, `data-lit` written straight onto the DOM node from the frame loop, dim when the timeline hasn't reached the lane); and the **time plane** the scrubber drags.

**`components/process/Flow.tsx`** (new) — one `Points` layer for heads plus **one mesh for all trails**. A trail is the flight path evaluated slightly in the past, so a ribbon costs one buffer write and no per-comet history. A run's history arrives in one burst, so comets leave a **launch queue at 10/s** — every logged event is seen to travel instead of flashing once. Arrivals report to the gates and queue rings. Under reduced motion the frame loop returns immediately and an effect places the most recent events as **still dots on their rails**, spaced by their position in the lane's work.

**`components/process/Director.tsx`** (new) — establishing move (cubic in-out, 2.5 s, high wide → working angle), slow drift while producing, pull-back framing every lane and the lit Integration gate when ended, gentle pan following the time plane while scrubbing, and a fixed angle under reduced motion. Touching the controls hands the camera over; it is taken back 12 s after the viewer lets go.

**`components/process/ProcessStage.tsx`** — assembly only. Holds the lanes still while events stream (`useLanes` re-publishes only when the lane set actually changes, so the rail mesh isn't rebuilt per event), derives per-gate arrivals and `merged`, and queues the one completion ring.

**`components/process/ProcessView.tsx`** — unchanged panel (timeline, event kinds, stream) plus a **Department lanes** key, and it now derives `completed` (`run.endedAt` present, or status `completed`, while at the head — or the event under the cursor is a merge) and `progress` for the scene.

**`components/process/process.module.css`** (new) — gate and lane label styling; lane labels are anchored left of the lane origin and read rightwards (`translateX(50%)`), which is what keeps them from clipping at the canvas edge at any camera pose.

## Frame time

Measured in dev at 1600×1000 through a temporary `FrameProbe` console line (40-frame windows), **removed before the first commit**. Headless Chromium here uses SwiftShader, so absolute numbers are software-rasteriser numbers dominated by the bloom pass; the ratio is the meaningful figure. Back-to-back on the same host, dropping each run's warm-up window:

- **before** (slab scene, 10 windows): mean **427.8 ms/frame**
- **after** (gates + rails + trails + camera, 9 windows): mean **442.4 ms/frame**
- **ratio 1.03×** — well inside the 1.5× budget.

(An earlier, less comparable baseline run measured 390.7 ms; the paired measurement above is the one to quote.) Dropping a redundant full-screen floor plane — the fog already resolved it to the background colour — took the first measured 1.25× down to 1.03×.

## Screenshots (all 1600×1000, read and iterated on)

| | Path |
| --- | --- |
| before, live feed | `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-deepseek-harness/f53f80cc-1f77-5d02-a862-99d59ffabdce/scratchpad/process/before/before-live.png` |
| before, replay fixture | `…/scratchpad/process/before/before-replay.png` |
| after, live, events in flight | `…/scratchpad/process/after/after-live-flow.png` |
| after, live, completed and settled | `…/scratchpad/process/after/after-live-settled.png` |
| after, live, timeline scrubbed back (time plane + pan) | `…/scratchpad/process/after/after-live-scrubbed.png` |
| after, replay fixture (merge ring breaking over Integration) | `…/scratchpad/process/after/after-replay.png` |
| after, reduced motion, live | `…/scratchpad/process/after/after-reduced-live.png` |
| after, reduced motion, replay | `…/scratchpad/process/after/after-reduced-replay.png` |

One caveat on "running": **every run the feed and the fixtures offer has an `endedAt`**, so no run on this host is still producing. The drift pose exists and is exercised by the same code path, but I could not photograph it honestly. If you want a "running" shot for the demo, start a review through the feed and screenshot while it streams.

## README sentences I would add

Under **The three views**, replacing the Process row's description:

> `2` | **Process** (`/process`) | The program pipeline as a lit corridor: each department lane is a glowing rail in its division's colour, running from the left edge through three tall glass gates — Verification, Judging, Integration — over a floor grid that recedes into the fog. Every logged event travels its lane as a comet with a ribbon trail, sized and coloured by kind; a certificate rings the Verification gate, a merge lights Integration and leaves it lit. A lane's label names the agent working it and its event count, and brightens while that agent is acting. The camera opens on an establishing move, drifts while the run produces, and pulls back to frame every lane once the run has ended. A timeline scrubber drags a time plane along the pipeline; `Head` returns to live.

And one sentence for **Limitations**:

> A run's recorded history reaches the deck in one burst, so the process view releases its comets from a queue at a fixed rate: every logged event is seen to travel, a few seconds after the panel has already counted it.

And appending to the reduced-motion sentence:

> In the process view it also stops the camera at one angle over the whole pipeline and stands each event as a still dot on its own rail instead of flying it.

## Shared change I need

**None blocking.** Two notes for whoever owns the shell:

1. `deck/camera.ts` did not exist in my branch point, so the Process camera lives in `components/process/Director.tsx`. If the shell agent lands a shared camera module with poses/easing, the Director should be folded onto it — its poses (`ESTABLISH`, `WORKING`, `FINISHED`, `STILL`) and its `cubic` ease are the obvious candidates, and the "viewer touched the controls, hand the camera over for 12 s" rule is worth sharing with the other two stages.
2. `components/three/Stage.tsx` hardcodes `dpr={[1, 1.75]}` and a fixed bloom. On a laptop GPU driving a boardroom screen the bloom pass is the dominant cost of all three views; if the shell agent wants headroom, that is the one dial to expose — my scene's own geometry costs ~3% of a frame.
